claims.feature: Customisable style rules saved as named profiles, shared as JSON
tests: ui:sql-formatter:2.7: named style profiles: save, switch, export and import as JSON
ui:sql-formatter:2.7: analysis finds the six problems and fixes each in one click
unit:sqlx:lint + fix: SELECT * becomes the column list when the table is known
unit:sqlx:lint + fix: UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE get a WHERE that matches nothing
unit:sqlx:lint + fix: NOT IN with a subquery excludes NULLs
unit:sqlx:lint + fix: an implicit join becomes an explicit JOIN ... ON
unit:sqlx:lint + fix: a declared variable that is never used is removed
unit:sqlx:lint: a leading wildcard in LIKE is reported, with no automatic fix

claims.feature: Bulk formatting and analysis of many files
tests: ui:sql-formatter:2.7: many files at once: formatted, zipped, errors listed per file
ui:sql-formatter:2.7: Format selection formats only the selected text
ui:sql-formatter:2.7: syntax checked in every dialect, with line and column
unit:sqlx:syntax: a real parser per dialect reports line, column and what it found

claims.feature: Autocomplete of tables and columns (from pasted DDL, no connection)
tests: ui:sql-formatter:2.7: autocomplete from pasted DDL: tables after FROM, columns after an alias
unit:sqlx:complete: tables after FROM/JOIN, columns after alias., columns of the tables in the query

gaps: Redgate SQL Prompt works inside SSMS and Visual Studio and completes code from your live database; Layerbit completes from DDL you paste and never connects to a database.
SQL Prompt refactors database objects (for example renaming one everywhere it is used); Layerbit formats and analyses text only.
